title: Intense training: the key to optimal performance before and during the taper
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: Moderately and highly trained subjects and athletes, with discussion of team sports
findings: Load reduction can be achieved by reducing intensity, volume and/or frequency, but with reduced training load there may be a risk of detraining.
Training at high intensities before the taper plays a key role in inducing maximal adaptations in moderately and highly trained subjects and athletes.
High-intensity training can also maintain or further enhance adaptations while athletes reduce training before a major competition.
Training volume can be markedly reduced without a negative impact on performance; training load should not be reduced at the expense of intensity during the taper.
limitations: Narrative review with no quantified effect sizes in the abstract; mixes endurance and team-sport evidence.
implications: Keep at least one quality session per week during the taper at pre-taper quality pace, with total volume shortened, rather than replacing quality with easy running (the count of one per week is an engine choice).
The final pre-taper block should contain intensity work; avoid entering a taper from a purely low-intensity base.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (Scand J Med Sci Sports, 14 Sep 2010). Journal name uses '&' in Crossref. Abstract has no numbers.
